key_insight: A lightweight test-time adaptation (TTA) framework applied to a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) preserves EMG gesture decoding accuracy under signal drift while keeping compute and memory low enough for on-device wearable use.
problem_solved: Surface EMG decoding performance degrades over time due to electrode shifts, muscle fatigue, and posture changes; existing fixes need large datasets or heavy compute pipelines that are impractical for energy-constrained wearables.
method: TCN-based EMG classifier paired with a compact online TTA loop that adapts model parameters at test time without labeled data.
Unsupervised adaptation objective (e.g., entropy/consistency style losses) applied per-sample or on small windows to correct drift with minimal computation and memory.
Design choices optimized for edge deployment: small model footprint, low update frequency, no large replay buffers or cloud dependence.
impact: Enables robust, long-term gesture recognition on resource-constrained wearable devices, reducing the need for extensive retraining or user recalibration while keeping power and latency low.
visual_elements: Schematic of wearable forearm EMG setup showing electrode drift over time (arrows) and resulting signal change.
Before/after line chart of accuracy across sessions: steep drop without adaptation vs stable performance with the lightweight TTA.
Block diagram: raw EMG → TCN classifier → lightweight TTA loop (unsupervised loss) → updated model (on-device).
Resource infographic: icons comparing model size, runtime, and power for baseline heavy methods vs proposed lightweight approach.
paper_title: Lightweight Test-Time Adaptation for EMG-Based Gesture Recognition
paper_authors: Nia Touko, Matthew O A Ellis, Cristiano Capone, Alessio Burrello, Elisa Donati
